heading: Open PDF Online: Free PDF Viewer
subtitle: Drop a PDF to read it page by page, search it and zoom in; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Open a PDF online in your browser: a free PDF viewer that shows every page in one scroll, with page thumbnails, zoom, fit to width and rotation. Search the text with highlights, select and copy it, Arabic included, and open password-protected PDFs by typing the password here. Your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your PDF is opened by your own browser and never sent to a server. A password you type is used only on this page.

features.title: Search and select
features.text: Find words across every page with highlighted matches, and select text to copy it, right to left for Arabic.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, PDFs keep opening without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: open a PDF online

steps.title: Drop your PDF on the page
steps.text: Choose or drop a .pdf file. It is read in your browser, never uploaded, and its pages appear in one scroll.

steps.title: Move around
steps.text: Click a thumbnail, type a page number, or scroll. Zoom in or out, fit the page to the width, or rotate it.

steps.title: Search and copy
steps.text: Press Ctrl+F (⌘F on a Mac) to search; matches are highlighted on the page. Select any text to copy it.

steps.title: Open a protected PDF
steps.text: If the PDF has a password, type it in the box that appears. It is used only in this tab and never stored.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the PDF itself and draws its pages on your screen. Nothing is sent to a server, so the file never leaves your device. To check, open your browser's network panel while you open a PDF and you will see no upload.

faq.question: Can I open a password-protected PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. A box asks for the password, and the PDF opens when it is right. The password is used only by this page in your browser: it is never stored or sent anywhere.

faq.question: Does it show Arabic PDFs correctly?
faq.answer: Yes. Pages are drawn exactly as the PDF lays them out, and Arabic text can be searched and selected in reading order, right to left.

faq.question: Why can't I select or search the text of a scanned PDF?
faq.answer: A scanned PDF is a picture of each page, with no text inside, so there is nothing to find or copy. OCR PDF reads the words on each page, in English or Arabic, and saves a copy you can search and select.

faq.question: Can I fill in or edit the PDF?
faq.answer: The OpenAnyDoc PDF viewer only shows the PDF, with any form fields and their values, and does not change it. To combine PDFs or number their pages, use Merge PDF or Add page numbers.

faq.question: Does it work on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes. It works in any modern browser on Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac and Linux, with no app to install. On a phone, the thumbnails open from the toolbar.

faq.question: What program opens a PDF file?
faq.answer: Every web browser opens a PDF file, on a computer or a phone, so no extra program is needed: Edge or Chrome on Windows, Preview or Safari on a Mac, and the Files or Books app on iPhone; Adobe Acrobat Reader is optional. OpenAnyDoc also opens PDFs in your browser, with thumbnails and search, without uploading them. More options are in how to open a PDF without Adobe.

faq.question: Why won't my PDF open?
faq.answer: A PDF usually won't open because it needs a password or because the file is damaged, often after a download or attachment that broke off. A password-protected PDF opens in the OpenAnyDoc viewer once you type the password, and Unlock PDF saves a copy without it; a damaged file can often be fixed with Repair PDF. If it opens but its text can't be searched, it is a scan, and OCR PDF adds the text.
